title: NodeGX node trace, format version 1
description: What a node did, in one form whichever implementation did it (phase 107, NSP-002). An ordered stream of stimulus events (set, in, settle, advance) and observation events (value, signal, outcome, request, open). Between two settles the observation events are grouped canonically: `value` events sorted by port name, then `signal` events in emission order, then `outcome` events in the order they were reported (NSP-007: an outcome the world settles — an answer landing, a timeout — is reported when it lands, which may be frames after its invocation), then `request` and `backend` events, one group, in the order they were issued, then the LOCATION group — `open`, `history`, `dispatch`, `stack`, `route` and `popup` events — in the order they were made (NSP-015); a `value` is recorded only when it changed since the last settle. Every event MAY carry a `subject` (what it happened to): omitted in a one-node trace, a node id in a graph trace, and left open for app-level subjects such as `app:click`. `completed` is never recorded: every `outcome` event implies it. A `failure` outcome carries the implementation's error CODE in `error`, never its message. Values are in the canonical form src/canonical.ts defines (tagged `$num` / `$date` objects for what JSON cannot say, keys sorted). The world (NSP-007, src/world.ts): `advance` says the scripted clock moved by `ms`; `request` says the node handed the world a request — `method` as handed, `url` as handed, `headers` with lower-cased names, `body` the text that travelled or `{ "$form": [[name, value], …] }` for form data, absent when there was none. NSP-015: `open` says the node asked the browser to open a URL (`window.open(url, target, features)`), each canonical, as handed; s17 `history` and `dispatch` the push and the event it dispatched; s18 `stack` a request handed to a Component Stack (src/world.ts STACK); s19 `route` a navigate handed to the Routers (src/world.ts ROUTE); s20 `popup` a popup shown or closed (src/world.ts POPUP). NSP-014 s21: `backend` says the node handed a backend an operation in the backend contract's words (src/world.ts BACKEND) — `op`, `backend` the id it went to, `args` as handed, callbacks left out.

port.description: A port name. MAY be empty: String Format registers the empty placeholder `{}` as the port named '' (NSP-006 found the schema refusing what the spec and its scenario produce).

canonical.description: A canonical value: JSON, plus `{ "$num": tag }` for -0 / NaN / ±Infinity and `{ "$date": iso | null }` for a Date. Key order is not expressible in JSON Schema; the TypeScript validator checks it.

oneOf.description: stimulus: a value written to an input port. `value` absent means undefined was written.
stimulus: the target drained its frame; the observations that follow belong to it.
observation: an output value changed (never undefined — C3).

observation: an outcome-reporting input finished (ERG-001) — `port` is the INPUT that was invoked; `''` (NSP-014 s29) when no input opened the invocation (an outcome a node reports for something that did not start on this page — Sign In With's return leg).
stimulus (NSP-007): the world's clock moved by `ms` milliseconds; every timer due on the way fired, in order.
observation (NSP-007): the node handed the world a request. `headers` names are lower-cased; `body` is the text that travelled, or `{ "$form": [[name, value], …] }`, or absent.

observation (NSP-015): the node asked the browser to open a URL — `window.open(url, target, features)` — each canonical, as handed; a target or features not handed is absent (s17). The world opens nothing (src/world.ts LOCATION).
observation (NSP-015 s17): the node pushed a history entry — `history.pushState(state, title, url)` — `url` canonical, as handed (src/world.ts LOCATION).
observation (NSP-015 s17): the node dispatched an event on the window — `window.dispatchEvent(event)` — named by its type (src/world.ts LOCATION).

observation (NSP-015 s18): the node handed a Component Stack a request (src/world.ts STACK) — `push` / `replace` (`NavigationHandler.navigate` / `.replace`: `stack` and `target` as handed, absent when not handed; `params` and `transition` canonical at the call) or `back` (a pop through the stack's back callback: `action` absent when none, `results` canonical at the call).

observation (NSP-015 s19): the node handed the Routers a navigate (src/world.ts ROUTE) — `RouterHandler.navigate(router, args)`: `router` and `target` as handed, absent when not handed; `params` and `openInNewTab` canonical at the call.

observation (NSP-015 s20): the popups (src/world.ts POPUP) — `show` (`context.showPopup(target, params, args)`, Show Popup: `target` as handed, `params` canonical at the call, `stackPolicy`, `closeOnEscape` and `modal` as handed, `accessibleName` absent when not handed) or `close` (the close handler a Close Popup resolved, called with `(action, results)`: `popup` the name of the popup it closes, absent when unnamed; `action` absent when none; `results` canonical at the call).

observation (NSP-014 s21): the node handed a backend an operation (src/world.ts BACKEND; R9, the request not the wire) — `op` the backend contract's method (`delete`, `query`, …), `backend` the id of the backend it went to, `args` the options as handed with callbacks left out, canonical at the call. In the request group.
